title: filter_range raises OpError when min > max instead of keeping no rows
spec_quote: `filter_range(field, min=None, max=None)`: keep rows whose numeric value lies within the inclusive bounds; at least one bound is required.
probe_note: filter_range([{a:1},{a:3}], field='a', min=5, max=1) must return []; anything else is DEFECT. Severity rationale: well-typed parameters, at least one bound given; the op sentence fixes the result (no row lies within) and the only parameter error it names is a missing bound.

title: Pipeline error prefix shows '?' instead of the given op when 'op' is not a string
spec_quote: a step is a dict `{"op": <name>, ...params}`; a failing step raises `OpError` whose message starts with `step <i> (<op>): `. Spec is silent on a non-string op (outside the defined step shape).
probe_note: run_pipeline([], [{'op': 5}]) must raise OpError whose message starts with 'step 1 (5): '.

title: Field-list parameters reject a repeated field name (drop, concat, ...)
spec_quote: `drop(fields)`: remove `fields`; a field a row lacks is ignored. / `concat(fields, into, sep="")`: join the string values of `fields` with `sep` into the new field `into`; a non-string value or an existing `into` raises `OpError`.
probe_note: drop([{a:1,b:2}], fields=['a','a']) must give [{b:2}] and concat([{a:'x'}], fields=['a','a'], into='b', sep='-') must give [{a:'x', b:'x-x'}]. A list of names with a repeat is the right type and the op sentences fix the result.

title: Field-list parameters reject an empty list (select, drop, concat, group_count)
spec_quote: `select(fields)`: keep only `fields` (a list of names), in that order. / `drop(fields)`: remove `fields` / `concat(fields, into, sep="")`: join the string values of `fields` with `sep` into the new field `into`; a non-string value or an existing `into` raises `OpError`. / `group_count(by, into="count")`: one row per distinct combination of the fields `by`
probe_note: With fields=[] / by=[] on two rows: select -> [{},{}], drop -> unchanged, concat into 'c' -> c == '' on each row, group_count -> [{count: 2}]. Any exception or different result is DEFECT.

title: rename rejects an empty mapping
spec_quote: `rename(mapping)`: `{old: new}`; the row keeps its field order; a `new` that equals another existing field of the row raises `OpError`.
probe_note: rename([{a:1}], mapping={}) must return [{a:1}]. An empty dict is the right type; the op sentence fixes the result (nothing renamed).

title: rename allows a new name equal to an existing field that is itself renamed (swap/chain)
spec_quote: a `new` that equals another existing field of the row raises `OpError`.
probe_note: rename([{a:1,b:2}], mapping={a:'b', b:'a'}) and mapping={a:'b', b:'c'} must both raise OpError (new 'b' equals the existing field 'b').

title: Operation run() makes rows positional-only; rows passed by keyword gives TypeError
spec_quote: Every operation lives in `dataops/ops/<name>.py` as `run(rows, **params) -> list[dict]` ... The interface is fixed.
probe_note: registry.get('select')(rows=[{a:1,b:2}], fields=['a']) must return [{a:1}]; the fixed signature run(rows, **params) accepts rows as a keyword.

title: cast to int rejects non-ASCII Unicode digit strings that match [+-]?\d+
spec_quote: `int`: from an int, a float with an integral value, or a string matching `[+-]?\d+` after stripping.
probe_note: cast on [{a:'\u0663'}, {a:' \u0661\u0662 '}, {a:'-\uff11\uff12'}] to int must give 3, 12, -12 (ints). In Python 3.9 re, \d on str matches every Unicode decimal digit and int() accepts them.

title: cast to int of a digit string over 4300 digits escapes as ValueError (CLI traceback) instead of OpError
spec_quote: a failing step raises `OpError` whose message starts with `step <i> (<op>): ` / every `OpError` exit with status 2 and one line on stderr, never a traceback.
probe_note: N/A when the interpreter has no int string-conversion limit (3.9.6). Else cast [{a:'1'*5000}] to int, directly and via run_pipeline: an exception other than OpError is DEFECT; returning an int or raising OpError is OK.

title: CLI prints a traceback when a valid result holds an int over 4300 digits
spec_quote: `python3 -m dataops PIPELINE.json INPUT.json` prints `json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)`. Spec is silent: json.dumps itself fails here on newer interpreters and the exit-2 rule covers only invalid files/input and OpError.
probe_note: N/A when no int string-conversion limit. Else CLI group_sum by ['g'] over 20 rows of a 4300-digit int: a traceback, an exit code other than 0/2, or exit 2 with more than one stderr line is DEFECT.

title: CLI accepts overflowing numbers (1e400) as infinity and prints non-JSON 'Infinity'
spec_quote: "Numeric" means `int` or `float` but not `bool`, and not NaN or infinity. Spec is silent on JSON number literals that overflow a float; 1e400 is valid JSON and the CLI does print json.dumps(result).
probe_note: CLI limit n=10 on [{a:1e400}] and fill value=1e999 on [{k:1}]: exit 0 with stdout that is not strict JSON (Infinity/NaN) is DEFECT; rejecting with exit 2 or printing finite JSON is OK.

title: join with non-scalar values in `other` crashes the CLI with a traceback
spec_quote: Unreadable or invalid JSON files, an input that is not a list of objects, and every `OpError` exit with status 2 and one line on stderr, never a traceback.
probe_note: CLI: join other=[{id:[1]}] / [{id:{a:1}}] on id; join other with v:[1,2] followed by dedupe, group_count by v, sort by v. Any traceback, exit not 0/2, or exit 2 without exactly one stderr line is DEFECT. (Non-scalar values are outside the spec; MAJOR only because the CLI crashes.)

title: join accepts non-scalar values in `other` and copies them into the output
spec_quote: Rows are a list of dicts (JSON objects) whose values are strings, numbers, booleans or `None`. / `other` is a list of rows. Non-scalar values are outside what the spec defines.
probe_note: get('join')([{k:1}], other=[{k:1, v:[1,2]}], on='k') and v:{x:1} must raise OpError; returning or another exception is DEFECT.

title: join checks for a shared non-`on` field only on matched pairs, not across both sides
spec_quote: A field other than `on` present on both sides raises `OpError`.
probe_note: join([{k:1,b:1}], other=[{k:2,b:2}], on='k') with how inner and left must raise OpError ('b' is present on both sides although no row matches).

title: group_sum (and group_stats) report 'not finite' when math.fsum overflows on an intermediate although the true sum is finite
spec_quote: The sum is an `int` when every summed value is an `int`, else a `float` computed with `math.fsum`; a sum that is not a finite float raises `OpError`. Spec is silent: math.fsum itself raises OverflowError on these values.
probe_note: group_sum by ['g'] over v = 1e308, 1e308, -1e308 must return [{g:1, sum:1e308}] (float); any exception or other result is DEFECT.

title: group_stats raises 'mean not finite' for large ints whose true mean is a finite float
spec_quote: `group_stats(by, field)`: as `group_sum`, adding the fields `count` (numeric values seen), `min`, `max` and `mean` ... a mean that is not a finite float raises `OpError`.
probe_note: group_stats by ['g'] over v = 10**308, 10**308 must return one row with count 2 and mean == 1e308 (finite float); an exception is DEFECT.

title: replace with a huge positive count (2**63) raises OverflowError instead of replacing
spec_quote: `replace(field, old, new, count=None)`: replace `old` by `new` in the string value, at most `count` times (a positive integer) when given / a failing step raises `OpError` whose message starts with `step <i> (<op>): `
probe_note: replace([{s:'aaa'}], field='s', old='a', new='b', count=2**63) and count=10**30 must return [{s:'bbb'}].

title: run_pipeline: a step dict with a non-string key raises TypeError instead of a prefixed OpError
spec_quote: a step is a dict `{"op": <name>, ...params}`; a failing step raises `OpError` whose message starts with `step <i> (<op>): `. Spec is silent on non-string parameter keys (impossible from JSON).
probe_note: run_pipeline([{a:1}], [{'op':'limit', 1:2, 'n':1}]) must raise OpError starting with 'step 1 (limit): '.

title: CLI refuses existing file paths that begin with '-' or '--'
spec_quote: `python3 -m dataops PIPELINE.json INPUT.json` prints `json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True)`; `python3 -m dataops --list` ... Spec is silent on how dash-prefixed arguments other than --list are parsed.
probe_note: In a temp dir holding '--p.json' and '-p.json' (limit n=5) and i.json, run `python -m dataops --p.json i.json` and `-p.json i.json`; each must exit 0 and print [{"a": 1}].

title: Unused imports in package modules (e.g. OpError imported but unused in ops)
spec_quote: Spec is silent (code quality).
probe_note: AST scan of dataops/**/*.py except __init__.py: an imported name never referenced as a Name and not in __all__ is DEFECT.

title: Helper code duplicated across modules (identical sum helper in group_sum and group_stats)
spec_quote: Spec is silent on code structure (step 1 only asks for 'the conventions the operations share').
probe_note: AST scan of dataops/**/*.py: two functions of 5+ lines in different files with identical arguments and body (docstring ignored) is DEFECT.

title: Operation modules mix absolute (dataops.x) and relative (..x) intra-package imports
spec_quote: Spec is silent (style).
probe_note: Over dataops/ops/<name>.py for the 20 ops: at least one module with an absolute dataops import and at least one with a relative import is DEFECT.

title: Unreachable error branch in fill (raise that no input can trigger)
spec_quote: Spec is silent (dead code).
probe_note: Heuristic: trace dataops/ops/fill.py while calling fill (registry and run_pipeline) with ~2,400 valid and invalid inputs (row shapes, field/value types, NaN/inf, missing/unknown params); any `raise` line never executed is DEFECT.

title: Missing deliverable (core module, ops module, doc page, test file, README, or registered op)
spec_quote: Every operation lives in `dataops/ops/<name>.py` ... `docs/ops/<name>.md` for every operation ... `tests/test_<name>.py` for every operation. ... 3. A README with the list of operations and one pipeline example.
probe_note: No review names a missing deliverable; included as the deliverable-existence check. DEFECT if dataops/{__init__,registry,pipeline}.py, README*, any dataops/ops/<name>.py, docs/ops/<name>.md or tests/test_<name>.py is missing, or registry.names() lacks one of the 20 ops.
